title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to the 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'. Grothendieck is studying a profinite group M. It is an extension 1 → 𝔊_0^+ → M → Γ̃_Q → 1. Here 𝔊_0^+ is (a version of) the profinite completion of SL2(Z) or PSL2(Z), the fundamental group of the modular stack M_{1,1}. Γ̃_Q is an extension or enlargement of the absolute Galois group Gal(Q̄/Q), in the spirit of GT. The two distinguished torsion elements are ρ_0 and σ_0. According to the next page their centralisers are Z/6 and Z/4, so they are the elliptic elements of order 6 and 4 generating SL2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6. They correspond to the two orbifold points j = 0 and j = 1728.

Previous page. Grothendieck built a group G_{ρ0,σ0} as an extension of a subgroup γ_{ρ0,σ0} ⊂ Γ̃_Q by 𝔊_0^{~+}. He showed that the induced map to M is injective (diagram (113)–(114)) and restricted it to a sub-extension G^♮_{ρ0,σ0}.

This page.
- (115): G^♮_{ρ0,σ0} ≅ M^♮, the subgroup of M defined by the conditions (107). It is an extension of γ_{ρ0,σ0} ↪ Γ̃_Q by 𝔊_0^♮. Hence M^♮ really is a subgroup of M.
- Marginal note (116), marked 'vérifier': γ_0 := γ_{ρ0,σ0} is the set of u ∈ Γ̃_Q admitting lifts to M that satisfy the conditions (107).
- (117)/(118): he defines a 'rigidified' group M^♮_{ρ0,σ0} = N_{M^♮}(ρ) ×_{γ0} N_{M^♮}(σ) ×_{γ0} M^♮. The factor N_{ρ0}^♮ = {u ∈ M^♮ | u(ρ) = ρ^{ε3(u)}} is the normaliser of the cyclic group ⟨ρ⟩, acting through the character ε3 : → (Z/6)^* = {±1}. Likewise N_{σ0}^♮ is the normaliser of ⟨σ⟩, with ε2 valued in (Z/4)^*. An element of M^♮_{ρ0,σ0} is thus a global automorphism together with compatible 'local' lifts that stabilise each elliptic conjugacy class representative.
- (119): there is an exact sequence 1 → SZ_{ρ0} × SZ_{σ0} → M^♮_{ρ0,σ0} → M^♮ → 1. The kernel is the product of the centralisers of ρ, σ in the geometric part, namely L_ρ × L_σ ≅ Z/6 × Z/4 (stated on the next page as (170)). It is 'tout petit', because the centraliser of an elliptic element in profinite SL2(Z) is just the finite cyclic group it generates.

Purpose. The next page goes on to cut out a still smaller extension of M^♮, by μ. The aim is a canonical 'base-point' rigidification of the Galois / GT-type action at the two orbifold points of M_{1,1}. This is analogous to tangential base points, but here it is achieved with normalisers of finite inertia.
errors: In (117) the first factor is written M^♮_{ρ0} but must be N^♮_{ρ0}, as the following definitions and (118) show; this is a slip of the pen.
In (117) the fibre products are over γ_{ρ0,σ0}, while in (118) they are over Γ_0^♮; the margin identifies these (Γ_0^♮ = γ_0), so this is notation, not a real discrepancy.

The exactness in (119) relies on two facts. First, N(ρ) → γ_0 has kernel equal to the centraliser of ρ in 𝔊_0^♮. Second, that centraliser equals ⟨ρ⟩ ≅ Z/6, which needs the profinite fact that centralisers of elliptic elements in profinite SL2(Z) are no bigger than in the discrete group. This is true (finite subgroups of profinite amalgams are conjugate into factors; Ribes–Zalesskii) but is not argued here. Surjectivity onto M^♮ also needs every u to normalise conjugates of ⟨ρ⟩ and ⟨σ⟩, i.e. preservation of the elliptic conjugacy classes. That presumably follows from (107) but is not shown.
Grothendieck himself flags the computation (116) with 'vérifier'.

ideas.what: Normaliser groups N_M(ρ), N_M(σ) of the elliptic torsion elements, with characters ε3, ε2 describing the action u(ρ)=ρ^{ε(u)}
ideas.modern_name: decomposition/inertia-type subgroups at the elliptic points of M_{1,1}; normalisers of finite subgroups in profinite SL2(Z)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara, Nakamura, Lochak–Schneps (Galois/GT action on profinite SL2(Z) and its torsion), 1990s
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the role of the modular stack M_{1,1} and its orbifold points; this explicit construction is not published

ideas.what: Fibre product N(ρ) ×_{γ0} N(σ) ×_{γ0} M as a rigidified extension of M^♮ by the finite group Z/6 × Z/4
ideas.modern_name: rigidification of an outer action by choosing compatible lifts at orbifold (elliptic) base points; extension by local inertia centralisers
ideas.usually_credited_to: no standard attribution; related ideas appear in work on GT acting on SL2(Z)^ and the genus-one Teichmüller tower (Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps, Hoshi–Mochizuki)

ideas.what: Injectivity of G_{ρ0,σ0} → M and the identification of M^♮ as a subgroup
ideas.modern_name: routine diagram chase in group extensions

missed.claim: Grothendieck constructs, step by step, an extension of the Galois/GT-type group M^♮ by the small finite group Z/6 × Z/4, and then (next page) by μ. This is obtained from normalisers of the order-6 and order-4 elliptic elements of profinite SL2(Z). It amounts to a canonical lifting of the outer action to an honest action rigidified at the two orbifold points of M_{1,1}. I am not aware of this 'elliptic-point base point' construction being written up in the literature in this form, as opposed to tangential base points at the cusp.
missed.quote: 1 → SZ_{ρ0} × SZ_{σ0} → M^♮_{ρ0,σ0} → M^♮ → 1 où le noyau ... est un groupe tout petit
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It could give an alternative description of the GT/Galois action on genus-one braid and modular groups, using the j=0 and j=1728 orbifold points as base points. This would be relevant to studies of GT acting on SL2(Z)^ and to the anabelian geometry of M_{1,1}.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful technical step in Grothendieck's unpublished study of the 'équation des lacets'. Rigidifying the Galois/GT action by normalisers of the elliptic elements of profinite SL2(Z) is natural, but not a standard published construction. Still, the page is mostly bookkeeping of fibre products and exact sequences, and its ingredients are close to known work.
transcription_corrections: 'est bien un (quo-[?]) groupe de M' should read 'est bien un sous-groupe de M'.
In (117) the first factor in the image appears as M_{ρ0}, an evident slip for N^♮_{ρ0}.
In (118) 'Γ^♮_0 ≠ γ_0' should read 'Γ^♮_0 =: γ_0' (a definition sign), not ≠.
In the margin, (116) defines γ_0 = γ_{ρ0,σ0} as {u ∈ Γ̃_Q | the lifts u_0 ∈ M of u satisfy the conditions (107)}; the word 'vérifier' with a downward arrow heads the note.
The page header number in the image is 685 (archive numbering); Grothendieck's own numbering continues on the next page as 646.
